ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows square ABCD, with A at the lower left corner, B at the lower right corner, C at the upper right corner, and D at the upper left corner. M is located near the midpoint of side AB, N is located on diagonal AC, segment MN connects from M to N, and the gray region is triangle MNC. Reasoning: By the coordinate method, suppose the side length of the square is 1, and take A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(1,1), D=(0,1). Because M is the midpoint of AB, M=(1/2,0). The equation of diagonal AC is y=x, and its slope is 1; MN is perpendicular to AC, so the slope of MN is -1. The equation of MN passing through M is y=-(x-1/2)=-x+1/2. Solving simultaneously with y=x gives x=-x+1/2, so x=1/4, y=1/4, therefore N=(1/4,1/4). The area of triangle MNC is 1/2 |det(N-M, C-M)|. Here N-M=(-1/4,1/4), C-M=(1/2,1), and the determinant is (-1/4)(1)-(1/4)(1/2)=-1/4-1/8=-3/8, so the area is 1/2·3/8=3/16. The area of the square is 1, so the ratio of the area of the gray triangle to the area of the square is 3/16:1=3:16.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate setup. First read the diagram: the shaded region is triangle MNC inside square ABCD, with A at bottom-left, B bottom-right, C top-right, D top-left; M lies halfway along AB and N lies on diagonal AC, with MN drawn to N. From the text, take ABCD as a square, M as the midpoint of AB, and MN perpendicular to AC. Set the square side length to 1, so A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(1,1), D=(0,1), and M=(1/2,0). Since AC is the line y=x and MN is perpendicular to it, the line through M has slope -1: y=-(x-1/2). Intersecting with y=x gives N=(1/4,1/4). Compute the area of triangle MNC using the determinant formula: area = 1/2 |det(N-M, C-M)| = 3/16. Since the square area is 1, the ratio is 3:16.
